newsitem.title: LEBANON: Beirut judge demands death for 3 Palestinians.
newsitem.headline: Beirut judge demands death for 3 Palestinians.

text.p: A Lebanese magistrate on Thursday demanded the death penalty for three radical Palestinian guerrillas charged with masterminding the 1993 assassination of the top PLO official in Beirut.
Magistrate Sa'eed Mirza charged the Fatah Revolutionary Council (FRC) members with planning the killing of Younis Awad, nom de guerre of the Palestine Liberation Organisation's Fatah official.

Mirza also ordered security forces to find out the real identity of Awad's alleged killer, named in the indictment as Sami Hamdan. Under Lebanese law a suspect can only be tried under his true identity.
Mirza did not set a date for the trial. Two of the FRC members are in custody.
Awad was shot dead in broad daylight on April 1, 1993 as he walked near his home in the Beirut suburb of Talet al-Khayyat.

Security sources said at the time that the killing was linked to the power struggle in Lebanon between Fatah and the FRC, which is led by guerrilla leader Sabri al-Banna, better known as Abu Nidal. Dozens were killed on both sides.
The FRC, which split from Fatah in 1973, is vehemently opposed to peace negotiations with Israel.
Fatah officials in Lebanon have also accused Abu Nidal followers of the November 1993 killing of Mouin Shabaytah, PLO leader Yasser Arafat's top official in Lebanon, near the southern port of Sidon.
